content: 1. In the past three months, have you received counseling on condom use and safe sex practices? This could include services provided by outreach programs, drop-in centers, or sexual health clinics. 2. Have you been tested for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in the last three months? This question is specifically directed at sex workers, transgender individuals, and men who have sex with men. 3. For individuals who inject drugs: Have you received new, sterile needles and syringes in the past three months? Data is disaggregated by gender (male, female, transgender) and age (<25 years, 25+ years). HIV Prevention Interventions The numerator is the number of individuals in key populations who received a defined, evidence-based package of HIV prevention interventions. The denominator is the estimated size of the key population group. For the denominator, validated population size estimates are used. For people who inject drugs, the prevention package must include access to sterile needles and syringes. The numerator is the number of sterile needles and syringes distributed by needle-syringe programs (NSPs) during the reporting period. The denominator can be either the estimated number of people who inject drugs in the country or the number of people reached by NSPs in the last 12 months. Data is collected through program records, such as NSP logbooks. The numerator is the number of people who inject drugs and are on OST at a specified date during the reporting period. The denominator is the number of opioid-dependent individuals in the country who inject drugs. Data is collected through program records, such as OST registers. The numerator is the number of survey respondents who reported using sterile needles and syringes during their last injection. The denominator is the total number of survey respondents. Data is collected through representative surveys of people who inject drugs. The numerator is the number of adolescent girls and young women seeking contraception or family planning services who were tested for HIV. The denominator is the total number of adolescent girls and young women seeking these services. Data is collected through program records, such as clinic registers. The numerator is the number of VMMCs performed according to national standards during the reporting period. Data is collected through program records, such as VMMC registers. The numerator is the number of males experiencing moderate or severe adverse events during or after circumcision surgery. The denominator is the total number of males undergoing VMMC during the reporting period. Data is collected through program records. Injection Safety in Healthcare Facilities This indicator assesses whether therapeutic injections are administered using new, disposable, single-use equipment. The numerator is the number of sampled healthcare facilities where all injections meet these criteria. The denominator is the total number of facilities sampled. Data is collected through health facility surveys. The numerator is the number of individuals screened for hepatitis C during the reporting period. The denominator is the total number of people living with HIV on ART during the reporting period. Data is collected through program records. The numerator is the number of individuals who initiated hepatitis C treatment during the reporting period. The denominator is the total number of individuals diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection. Data is collected through program records and/or modeled estimates. The numerator is the number of individuals screened for TB during the reporting period. The denominator is the total number of individuals newly initiated on ART during the reporting period. Data is collected through program records, such as ART registers. TB Diagnosis and Treatment Indicators track the percentage of individuals screened for TB symptoms who test positive, are diagnosed with active TB, and initiate TB treatment. Data is collected through program records, and disaggregation includes gender and age. These indicators collectively provide critical insights into the effectiveness of HIV, TB, and hepatitis C prevention and treatment programs, as well as the safety of medical practices.
